html:
Petar II Petrović-Njegoš was prince-bishop of Montenegro from 1830 to 1851 and its greatest poet, born in 1813 in the village of Njeguši.

He set up a senate, courts and the first taxes, trying to turn a land of clans into a state. He fought the Ottomans and visited Russia and Vienna for support. His epic The Mountain Wreath, of 1847, tells of Montenegrins killing their kinsmen who had converted to Islam, and is still read and argued over. It is a classic of Serbian and Montenegrin literature. He died of tuberculosis at 37 and is buried in a mausoleum on Mount Lovćen, between Cetinje and the Bay of Kotor, the symbol of Montenegro.
sum: Petar II Petrović-Njegoš was prince-bishop of Montenegro from 1830 to 1851 and its greatest poet, born in 1813 in the village of Njeguši.
